title: Kindergarten phonemic awareness
label: SYNTHETIC — not a real classroom

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: What sound do you hear at the beginning of sun? Everybody.

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: Good. Now mop. Jaylen code A1, what sound?

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: How do you know it is /m/? Say the word slowly.

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: mmm-op. I hear mmm first.

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: Turn to your partner and find the first sound in fish.

segments.speaker: group
segments.text: /f/ fish /f/

notes: Group answers must not be counted as individual mastery.

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: Why do you think the fox tricked the crow? Student 1?

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: Because he wanted the cheese and he knew the crow liked compliments.

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: What in the story tells you the crow liked compliments?

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: It said she puffed up her feathers when he said she was beautiful.

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: Student 2, do you agree?

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: Yes.

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: Why?

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: Because he said so.

title: Grade 4 mathematics — misconception-rich fraction discussion
label: SYNTHETIC — not a real classroom

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: Which is bigger, one third or one fourth? Show me with your hands and explain. Student 1.

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: One fourth, because four is bigger than three.

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: Interesting. Student 2, same or different?

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: Different. If you cut a pizza into four you get smaller pieces, so one third is bigger.

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: Student 1, what do you think about that pizza idea?

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: Oh. The pieces are smaller. But the number is bigger so I was confused.

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: Everyone, with your partner: is one fifth bigger or smaller than one third, and why?

segments.speaker: group
segments.text: smaller smaller because more pieces

notes: Classic whole-number-reasoning misconception; competing explanation should be offered.

title: Grade 6 science
label: SYNTHETIC — not a real classroom

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: Before we heat the water, predict: what will happen to the particles? Write it, then tell your table.

segments.speaker: unknown
segments.text: [inaudible] table talk

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: Student 3, what did your table predict?

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: The particles will get bigger when it gets hot.

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: Get bigger, or something else changes? What did the simulation show yesterday?

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: They moved faster and spread out. So not bigger, farther apart.

notes: Inaudible table talk must stay unknown, not attributed.

segments.text: Today I am going to explain the three causes of the war. The first cause was economic. ... The second cause ... The third cause ... Any questions? No? Good.

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: No.

notes: Documented explicit modelling phase: context note applies (F26) but zero CFU is still a finding.

title: Grade 8 ELA — student-led discussion
label: SYNTHETIC — not a real classroom

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: Student 1, you are leading. Go ahead.

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: I think the theme is that power isolates people. On page 40 she says she has no one left to tell the truth to. Student 4, you disagreed.

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: I do not disagree, I think it is more specific. It is that power makes people lie to themselves. The mirror scene shows that.

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: Can I add to that? The mirror scene is where she actually says the truth for once, so maybe both.

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: Say more about how both could be true at the same time.

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: Isolation comes first and then she lies to herself because nobody corrects her.

notes: Strong student talk with rigour; band 5 is defensible only with cognitive rigour evidence.

title: Algebra I — strong student talk, weak learning
label: SYNTHETIC — not a real classroom

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: Solve 3x plus 5 equals 20 with your partner and explain each step.

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: You add five to both sides, so 3x equals 25, then divide, x is like 8.3.

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: Yeah I got that too, 8.3.

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: Mine was 8.33 so same thing.

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: Great discussion everyone, move on to number two.

notes: High participation with a shared procedural error the teacher did not catch (F35).

title: Geometry — limited talk with strong independent work
label: SYNTHETIC — not a real classroom

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: Prove the base angles of an isosceles triangle are congruent. Twelve minutes. I will circulate.

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: Student 5, your auxiliary line choice is interesting. Why the median?

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: Because then I get SSS with the shared side, which gives me the angles by CPCTC.

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: Nice. Keep going.

notes: Silence is productive here (F27); audio cannot score task engagement (F31).

title: High school history — misaligned questioning
label: SYNTHETIC — not a real classroom

context.subject: US History
context.standard: Evaluate the causes of the Great Depression

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: What year did the stock market crash?

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: And who was president?

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: Hoover

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: What did people call the shanty towns?

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: Hoovervilles

notes: Recall questions that sound historical are still DOK 1 (F19/F22/F23).

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: Student 2, read me your reason sentence.

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: Dogs are good because they are good.

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: You have a claim and a reason word, because. Right now the reason repeats the claim. Give me one fact about dogs that supports good.

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: Dogs can be trained to help blind people.

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: Now put that after because and read it again.

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: Dogs are good because they can be trained to help blind people.

title: Multilingual classroom discussion with code-switching
label: SYNTHETIC — not a real classroom

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: How many legs on four dogs? Explain to your partner, you can use Spanish or English.

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: Cuatro perros, each one tiene four legs, so four times four, dieciséis.

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: Student 1, say your thinking for everyone.

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: Four groups of four. Sixteen.

notes: Preserve code-switching verbatim; do not correct it (F15).

title: Strong instructional improvement after coaching (follow-up)
label: SYNTHETIC — not a real classroom

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: Is this table proportional? Thumbs are not enough today: Student 3, how do you know?

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: Every y divided by x is 4, and when x is zero y is zero.

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: Student 6, could it still be proportional if it did not go through zero?

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: No, because then it is not a constant ratio from the start, it is y equals mx plus b with a b.

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: Everyone write one sentence: proportional means ... Student 1, read yours.

segments.speaker: student
segments.text: Proportional means constant ratio and through the origin.

segments.speaker: teacher
segments.text: Exit ticket: table 4, is it proportional and how do you know? Two sentences.

notes: Compare with the baseline fixture to show adult behaviour change → student response.
